title: Wash-sale adjustment math is correct but presentation is terse

verification.note: Positive. 10 of 18 disposed shares had a replacement purchase inside the window; 3.60 of the 6.48 loss was disallowed pro rata, rolled into the replacement lot's basis, and the holding period tolled. The API exposed replacement_txn_ids, replacement_lot_ids, basis_added_to_lot_id and holding_period_tolled_to.

why_it_matters: This is exactly the calculation that most tax software gets wrong. The app got it right. The $3.60 is not lost; it will reduce the gain (or increase the loss) on a future sale of the 08-04 lot. The holding-period toll prevents a short-term loss on the original sale from becoming a long-term gain on an immediate buyback. The application's tax machinery works correctly here, and the API provides enough detail to verify the calculation.

repro: observe: total_cost_basis and total_market_value present, but no cash or total_equity fields
title: Portfolio endpoint lacks cash and total equity

verification.note: Same root cause as the cash gap: with no cash figure there is no equity figure, so period performance cannot be computed from the API at all.

why_it_matters: A professional investor conducting week-in-review cannot answer the fundamental question 'what did this sleeve make?' because the portfolio endpoint only shows position totals, not total account value. This blocks the primary use case for end-of-week reporting.

expected: A trade history endpoint should return all trades (buys and sells) in chronological order. Alternatively, the portfolio or activity page should show complete transaction history.
observed: GET /api/tax/report?year=2026 returns form8949 with 1 row (XLE sale on 2026-08-06). The 5 buy trades executed this week are not in the response.
repro: observe: form8949.rows has 1 element (the XLE sale)
no endpoint returns the 5 buy trades
title: Trade history shows only sales, not purchases

verification.note: Confirmed and understated. There is no transaction or activity endpoint anywhere in the API -- the only route under /api/portfolio is the positions report. The buys are not 'hidden'; nothing has ever exposed them. Notable because provenance-to-the-CSV-row is the application's stated design premise.

why_it_matters: A professional reviewing the week has no way to list what they bought, when, at what price, or their current holdings basis without reading the brokerage statement directly. The app blocks the 'what did I trade?' question in week-in-review.

expected: Portfolio endpoint should return cash decomposed as settled and unsettled so the UI can display 'Unsettled: $1,050' for the XLE trim proceeds pending settlement.
observed: GET /api/portfolio returns no cash, settled_cash, or unsettled fields. The harness brief command shows settled_cash separately, but the portfolio API/page cannot display it.
repro: run brief command: shows settled_cash 3017.88 and cash 4068.33
observe: no cash fields in the response
title: Portfolio API does not expose unsettled vs settled cash

verification.note: Settled-versus-unsettled is a stronger claim than the cash gap and is equally true: the ledger records trade and settle dates per transaction, so the distinction is derivable, but nothing computes or exposes it.

why_it_matters: Alex has $1,050 unsettled from Thursday's trim and must know it is unavailable for Monday trading. Not distinguishing settled from unsettled cash creates the risk of double-counting available capital or attempting trades with unavailable proceeds.

expected: When a user requests tax data for a year with no transactions, the page should display 'No transactions in 2019' or similar, not a blank panel.
observed: GET /api/tax/report?year=2019 returns a valid empty structure (gains.rows=[]), but the UI likely renders as a blank panel with no guidance text.
repro: Navigate to Tax page (blocked by browser rendering issue, but confirmed via API)
title: Empty tax year renders as blank panel with no explanation

verification.note: Plausible and low cost to check, but not verified against Tax.tsx this pass.

why_it_matters: Per Alex's persona, a blank panel is a bug report. A user cannot tell if the page is loading, errored, or correctly showing no data.

expected: Prices should be dated as of today or the most recent available market close, never future dates. Price timestamp must be accurate to the minute so calculations are valid.
observed: GET /api/portfolio returns positions with 'price_as_of':'2026-08-11', which is 4 trading days after the session trading date of 2026-08-07. Market value and unrealized gains use these future prices.
title: Portfolio prices are 4 days in the future

verification.note: Duplicate of portfolio-prices-7-days-future. Same harness artifact.

why_it_matters: Alex's persona: 'A price with no timestamp is unusable. A total that silently mixes a stale close with a fresh one is worse than no total.' Future-dated prices silently corrupt P&L calculations and violate the fundamental 'every figure carries an as-of' principle.

expected: Home page should guide a new user: link to documentation, button to import broker data, or wizard to connect brokerage account.
observed: Portfolio page (home / default route) displays store status grid (Accounts=0, Instruments=0, etc.) and text: 'No derived positions yet. Drop broker exports into data/ and rebuild.' No link, no button, no guidance.
repro: Empty ledger state (confirmed via code review)
Portfolio page renders placeholder with data/ directory mention
title: Home page lacks onboarding for new users

verification.note: The empty state does exist and names the supported brokers, so the page is not blank. What it asks the user to do -- drop files into data/ on the server's filesystem -- has no UI affordance anywhere, which is the substance of the complaint.

why_it_matters: A professional opening the app for the first time has no clear path to start. The message 'drop into data/' is developer guidance, not user guidance. Empty apps must have designed onboarding, not blank panels.
